headline: BNP leader shot dead by gunmen in Khulna
summary: Rafiqul Islam, a member of the Botiaghata Upazila BNP convener committee, was killed in the city's Labonchara area on Friday.
details: Rafiqul Islam, a 35-year-old BNP leader, was shot dead by gunmen in Khulna on Friday afternoon.
The incident occurred around 12:30 PM at Kazipara Bazar in the Mathabhanga area under Labonchara Police Station.
Islam was a member of the Botiaghata Upazila BNP convener committee and a resident of Jalma Union in Botiaghata Upazila.
He was also known as 'Dhakaia Rafiq' and previously served as the joint general secretary of the Fatullah Police Station volunteer team.
caption:
A 35-year-old BNP leader was shot dead by gunmen in broad daylight in Khulna.

Rafiqul Islam, a 35-year-old BNP leader, was shot dead by gunmen in Khulna on Friday afternoon.

The incident occurred around 12:30 PM at Kazipara Bazar in the Mathabhanga area under Labonchara Police Station.

Islam was a member of the Botiaghata Upazila BNP convener committee and a resident of Jalma Union in Botiaghata Upazila.

He was also known as 'Dhakaia Rafiq' and previously served as the joint general secretary of the Fatullah Police Station volunteer team.

#Khulna #BNP #Bangladesh #CrimeNews #Politics

Source: Prothom Alo

headline_marked: CPD warns [[spending without productivity may stoke inflation]] in new budget
headline: CPD warns spending without productivity may stoke inflation in new budget
summary: The Centre for Policy Dialogue cautions that the government's Tk 938,000 crore budget could fuel price hikes if public spending fails to generate higher investment and employment.
details: The Centre for Policy Dialogue (CPD) has cautioned that the government's ambitious spending plans for the next fiscal year could increase inflationary pressures if the expenditure fails to generate productivity gains.
Finance Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury placed a Tk 938,000 crore budget for the next fiscal year, an outlay that is 18.7 percent higher year on year.
The government targets to bring down annual average inflation to 7.5 percent, but CPD warns this will be difficult unless public spending translates into higher investment, employment, and output.
According to CPD, inflation remains largely supply-driven, meaning controlling prices will require measures beyond monetary tightening, including ensuring affordable food and energy supplies.
The think tank also questioned the government's GDP growth target of 6.5 percent, noting that private investment and credit growth have remained sluggish in recent years.
CPD emphasized that the success of the budget will depend less on its size than on the quality of execution and the strength of institutions capable of delivering tangible outcomes.
caption:
Can a Tk 938,000 crore budget actually lower inflation? CPD warns that without productivity gains, it might do the opposite.

The Centre for Policy Dialogue (CPD) has cautioned that the government's ambitious spending plans for the next fiscal year could increase inflationary pressures if the expenditure fails to generate productivity gains.

Finance Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury placed a Tk 938,000 crore budget for the next fiscal year, an outlay that is 18.7 percent higher year on year.

The government targets to bring down annual average inflation to 7.5 percent, but CPD warns this will be difficult unless public spending translates into higher investment, employment, and output.

According to CPD, inflation remains largely supply-driven, meaning controlling prices will require measures beyond monetary tightening, including ensuring affordable food and energy supplies.

The think tank also questioned the government's GDP growth target of 6.5 percent, noting that private investment and credit growth have remained sluggish in recent years.

CPD emphasized that the success of the budget will depend less on its size than on the quality of execution and the strength of institutions capable of delivering tangible outcomes.

#Bangladesh #Budget2026 #Economy #Inflation #CPD #News

Source: Jamuna TV, Somoy News, The Daily Star, Prothom Alo
